parsed.basis: Liberia criminalises consensual same-sex conduct with up to one year imprisonment, enforcement is uncommon but the law deters reporting and has been used to arrest LGBTQ people after attacks, and gender-affirming care is unavailable. Advocacy-linked private spaces exist mainly through organisations in larger centres, while public concealment is the norm. River Gee is a remote, rural south-eastern county far from Monrovia, with limited tourism and a sparse institutional presence, so advocacy, legal assistance and independent recourse are distant or thin. Local communities are socially conservative and traditional, increasing risk of exposure, confrontation and community-level hostility if a visitor is identified as transgender, with fewer practical avenues for protection or remedy after discovery.
